headline: Hidden Forest Near Manila Shelters Rare Plants Against Urban Sprawl
meta_description: A mountainous reserve near Manila harbors 294 plant species, including 42 found only in the Philippines, despite pressure from urbanization.
summary_short: A forest reserve south of Manila protects rare plants in the shadow of one of Asia's most urbanized regions—but time is running out.
body:
Mounts Palay-Palay-Mataas-na-Gulod Protected Landscape, a mountainous reserve on the southern shores of Manila Bay, stands as an unexpected sanctuary for Philippine biodiversity. A 2016 survey documented 294 plant species across the landscape's varied habitats, with 42 species—roughly one in six—found nowhere else on Earth. Among the threatened species catalogued were 31 plants on national or international red lists, underscoring the landscape's irreplaceable ecological value. The discovery proved striking: this last remnant of natural lowland forest in Cavite province maintains an exceptionally high concentration of biodiversity despite sitting within arm's reach of one of Asia's most densely populated metropolitan areas.

Perhaps most encouraging was the dominance of guijo, a critically endangered tree, in the forest's interior core—evidence of a promising resurgence. Yet that same decade-long baseline has become a warning. Satellite imagery reveals that between 2015 and 2021, the protected landscape lost 13.8 percent of its forested area to urbanization and land conversion. The breach of strict protection zones suggests that the fragile recovery documented in 2016 may already be stalling.

Researchers stress that the 10-year gap since the last comprehensive survey highlights a critical need: continuous monitoring rather than isolated snapshots. Establishing permanent monitoring plots could track how this ecosystem functions as climate change and urban pressure mount. The authors call for urgent policy interventions and aggressive conservation programs to prevent the endemic and threatened plants from being permanently lost to fragmentation. Without sustained attention, a forest that survived so close to a megacity may not survive the next decade.
quick_facts: 294 plant species documented in 2016 forest survey near Manila
42 species found only in the Philippines—16% of total surveyed
13.8% forest loss between 2015 and 2021 due to urbanization
Guijo tree showing rare resurgence in protected landscape interior
